answer: Because the velvet index resolves every citation against the harbor checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the lagoon audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 139 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 139 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 2410 identities would post 1505 proofs and burn roughly 32 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
